decisions.executionNote: Raise and turn the right gripper toward the basket, with small continuous elbow-up movements; left arm stays home.
Approach above the basket's back-right egg while rotating the fingers downward, maintaining clearance.
Lower the open right fingers around the back-right egg; use the wrist view to refine grasp height.
Center slightly, close on the egg, and make a short test lift; retention must be checked visually.
Lift the apparently retained first egg clear of the rim, then travel toward the holder with the gripper kept closed.
Carry the first egg above the holder's right-back socket and angle the tool inward without crossing arms.
The wrist image no longer shows a retained egg. Return open above the basket for a better-centered vertical grasp.
Align the open fingers vertically over the back-right egg and descend cautiously; all four eggs are visible in the basket.
Lower the fingertips around the egg's sides before fully closing; make only a small test lift.
The egg appears forward of the finger pads. Reopen, shift toward its center, and close again at a lower side grasp.
Test a straight vertical lift with the fingers closed, avoiding rotation until egg retention is confirmed visually.
The egg is still between the fingers after the lift. Carry it toward the holder slowly, with a modest inward tilt and closed grip.
Continue toward the right socket, keeping the retained egg closed and moving gently inward and down.
Align the egg over the back-right cup and lower it gradually, keeping the tool on the right side of center.
Back away slightly from the lid while seating the egg over the rear cup, then release and lift to inspect. Contact has limited downward tracking.
One egg is visibly in the holder. Lift clear and return above the leftmost basket egg with the fingers open and pointed downward.
Descend vertically with open fingers around the isolated leftmost egg; inspect alignment before closing.
Close around the centered egg without pushing farther into the basket, then perform a short vertical retention test.
The egg remained in the basket. Reopen and lower the finger pads farther around its sides before another grasp.
The egg rolled toward the basket front. Follow its new position with a narrower approach clear of the rim, then close around its sides.
Lift vertically with the grip closed to see whether the shifted egg is securely retained, without adding lateral motion.
The last lift was empty. Recenter over the leftmost egg's new front position and lower open pads below its widest point.
Close on the egg now centered between the lower pads, then test a small straight lift before transporting.
The grip is empty. Recenter slightly right and lower the open pads more deeply around the front egg rather than closing above it.
Close at the deeper position and lift straight up, checking the egg rather than the gripper command for retention.
The front egg is not retained and is against the rim. Reposition over the isolated rear egg with a more vertical, open approach.
Lower slowly over the isolated back egg, correcting slightly left and forward, and inspect the pad alignment before closure.
Close around the rear egg now centered between the pads, with a tiny settling motion, then test a vertical lift.
The egg rolled forward instead of lifting. Move the open grasp center forward to match its observed position, then descend without closing yet.
The egg is centered between open jaws. Set the pads slightly deeper, close fully, and test a short lift with no sideways motion.
The egg appears retained between the pads. Lift clear before carrying toward the holder's open front-right cup.
Carry the retained egg above the front-right socket, staying in front of the partly lowered lid and tilting inward gradually.
The lid has fallen closed. Keep the egg secure to the right and bring the left arm up to reopen the lid without crossing arms.
Approach the lid with the left gripper, rotating its pinch direction to straddle the front edge. Right holds the egg stationary.
Position the left fingers above the lid's front-left edge, with the pinch axis nearly front-to-back; keep the egg safely stationary.
Try pinching the lid's front edge with the left fingers and lifting gently; the right hand continues holding the egg.
Test whether the left grasp engages the lid by lifting along its opening arc; watch for whole-holder motion or a slip.
The lid grasp slipped. Retract the left hand toward the front and reorient for a horizontal pinch of the lid lip, while retaining the egg on the right.
Bring the left gripper horizontally toward the front lip, keeping the elbow-up branch and the right egg stationary.
Replan the interrupted left motion using much smaller rotations. The right egg has slipped onto the table; clear that hand while finishing the lid approach.
Set the left vertical pinch onto the lid's front lip with a small inward insertion, then close without further lowering.
Lift the engaged front lip gently along an opening arc while watching whether the lid separates from the base.
The lid is separating from the base. Continue lifting its front lip backward along the hinge arc while keeping the left grip closed.
Continue reopening toward vertical, moving the held lip backward so the left hand can keep the lid out of the egg-placement path.
Keep the reopened lid held with the left hand. Move the right open gripper vertically above the egg on the table.
Lower the right fingers around the table egg, correcting leftward alignment; the left hand keeps the lid open.
Descent was obstructed near the holder. Replan from the observed pose: shift right, narrow the opening, and tilt inward for clearance.
Use a tiny recovery step to restore target continuity, then shift outward slowly while narrowing the fingers.
Descend from the cleared outward approach toward the table egg with a moderate opening; left continues holding the lid.
Correct the table egg's rightward offset between the jaws, close around its sides, and make a short test lift.
The fingers closed short of the egg. Reopen and advance along the tool axis so the pads reach its sides rather than its top.
Shift the right pads outward to clear the holder wall, narrow their opening, and lower another small amount around the table egg.
Contact is preventing the tilted grasp from lowering. Lift clear and level the two pads for a vertical approach to the table egg.
Center the now-level pads over the table egg and lower vertically, keeping the opening narrow enough to clear the holder.
Close the level pads around the centered table egg and make a straight test lift, while keeping the lid held open.
Follow the egg's new front-left position and approach its equator with level fingers, leaving the holder wall behind the grasp.
Close the pads on the now-centered egg at the deeper position and lift vertically to verify retention.
The table egg is being squeezed out by a shallow grasp. Follow it forward and lower the open pads substantially closer to table level before closing.
Close at the table-limited deeper height with a slight rightward centering correction, then lift only vertically to check retention.
The table egg is retained. Lift clear and carry it directly above the front-right socket while the left hand holds the lid open.
Lower the retained egg into the front-right cup with a small inward alignment correction, staying below the left wrist.
The egg slipped onto the table again. Clear the right wrist and push the held lid farther past vertical so the left arm can withdraw from the placement path.
Withdraw the left hand from the now-open lid. Reorient the right pads vertically above the relocated table egg for a deeper grasp.
Lower the vertical right fingers toward table-level contact around the egg, with the left arm now safely clear.
The basket rim appears to block the right jaw. Lift clear and turn the pinch axis front-to-back to avoid the narrow space beside the basket.
Finish turning the open fingers above the rim so they can approach the egg along its narrow axis without hitting the basket.
Align the front-to-back pinch over the table egg and descend vertically with the basket rim outside the jaws.
The basket blocks the approach. Retract forward and upward to clear the rim, narrowing the fingers before reorienting.
Reorient to level downward pads while approaching the table egg from the clear front side.
Continue from the interrupted pose with half-size wrist turns and small translation increments.
Advance the vertical pads to the egg, which is ahead of the grasp center in the wrist image, and lower cautiously.
The wrist is blocked by the basket on a vertical approach. Retract toward the front and tilt the fingers forward so the wrist can remain clear of the rim.
First restore continuity with a tiny correction, then withdraw from the basket and turn to a front-side approach.
Lower from the front with the fingers angled toward the egg, keeping the wrist behind the basket rim.
